NO, AND THIS IS THE STEP THAT FAILS. 2.000 mol of thionyl chloride is 3.149 equivalents against 0.6351 mol of the compound the paragraph names, and that compound is the acid chloride: it has no hydroxyl for the thionyl chloride to substitute, so on the printed reading the entire 237.9 g is charged onto a substrate that cannot consume it and is then stripped off again as 'the excess'.
